body.name: step-indexed denominator certificate ledger
body.construction:
The ledger is an ordered list.  Entry \(j\) contains a denominator circuit \(d_j\), its context-initialization, truncated-factorization, or fixing origin, a list of dependencies with indices smaller than \(j\), an exact cross-multiplied identity, a nonempty set of branch-reachable positive cells, and a positivity derivation.  A base entry is
\[
 d_j=p_H(S=s)=\sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^{+})}p_H(v,s),
 \qquad s\in H.
\]
Every conditioning denominator used by \(\operatorname{TF}_{\prec}\) is its actual marginal.  Every fixing denominator is first constructed from current-kernel marginals, after which the successor identity is recorded by cross-multiplication.  Following substitution into \(p_H\), cancellation, and sign normalization, each nonbase denominator must carry a verified factorization into a positive rational constant, earlier ledger entries, and nonempty sums of branch-reachable positive kernel cells.  The terminal registry \(\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}}\) is the ordered list of the denominator circuits that occur in the emitted reduced formula. The ledger is append-only for a run and retains every actual divisor, even when algebraic cancellation removes it from the final reduced circuit.
